design_principles.stability: Orthogonal axes; confidence-weighted aggregation; preserve past information.
design_principles.scalability: Append-only growth: new layers/questions can be added without changing existing IDs.

confidence_ui.prompt: How confident are you in this answer?

axis_aggregation.name: confidence_weighted_mean
rationale: Down-weights uncertain answers to reduce noise and identity drift.
Allows refinement without overwriting: higher-confidence future data can dominate naturally.
Improves temporal stability and preserves informational continuity.

axis_confidence.note: Future versions can add variance-aware confidence; v1 uses mean for simplicity.

append_only_policy.rule: Never reuse or change an existing axis_id/question_id. Add new items with new IDs only.
append_only_policy.reason: Prevents dataset corruption and keeps historical compatibility.

scope.purpose: Capture observer-perceived expressive qualities using scenario-based adjective selection. Stored qualitatively as adjective frequencies per axis with scenario labels and optional observer notes.

aggregation.rule: For each axis, count each selected adjective once per question selection. Store counts and scenario labels; do not compute a numeric axis score.

axes.name: Humor ↔ Seriousness
axes.definition: How the person comes across in terms of humor vs seriousness in everyday interactions.

questions.scenario_text: You’re having a casual conversation with this person in a relaxed setting. What does it feel like?
Something awkward or mildly uncomfortable happens during a group interaction. How would this person behave?
They are telling a story about something that happened to them. What is the vibe of the story?

axes.name: Warmth ↔ Coolness
axes.definition: How warm, friendly, and approachable the person seems versus distant or detached.

questions.scenario_text: You introduce this person to someone new. What is their attitude?
Someone shares a small personal concern with them. How would this person behave?
They greet people they already know in the ways that are?

axes.name: Directness ↔ Diplomacy
axes.definition: How direct/blunt the person seems versus tactful/diplomatic in communication.

questions.scenario_text: They disagree with someone in conversation. What is their attitude?
They need to point out a mistake someone made. They would do this in ways that are
They’re giving feedback in a sensitive situation. How would this person behave?

axes.name: Energy ↔ Calm
axes.definition: How energetic/intense the person seems versus calm/low-key in presence.

questions.scenario_text: They enter a room where people are already talking. How would they feel?
You spend several hours with this person. How would you feel?
Things become hectic or busy around them in the ways that are

axes.name: Expressiveness ↔ Composure
axes.definition: How emotionally expressive/open the person appears versus composed/controlled/hard-to-read.

questions.scenario_text: They react to good news in which ways?
They react to disappointing news in which ways?
During everyday conversation, their emotions are usually:

axes.name: Formality ↔ Casualness
axes.definition: How formal/structured the person seems versus casual/relaxed in style and manner.

questions.scenario_text: They’re talking in a social setting in what ways?
They meet someone they don’t know very well. How would they greet them?
They’re communicating in a more serious or official situation. What is their style?

output.description: Objective adjective frequencies per axis with scenario labels and optional observer notes. No numeric axis value is produced.

usage_rules: Use these adjectives as observed expressive tendencies in similar scenarios.
Do not fabricate adjectives beyond what is listed; lean on higher-frequency counts first.
If multiple adjectives tie, pick ones consistent with other layers’ signals.

scope.purpose: Store observer-known background information to ground the persona for realistic LLM behavior. This layer is qualitative only (no numeric scoring).
non_goals: Appearance capture (handled elsewhere via image input and other layers)
Personality scoring or trait inference (handled by Layers 1–4)

input_guidance.observer_rule: Answer only what you personally know or have directly observed. If you are unsure, write 'Not sure'.
